action: Operators of the listed Siemens and Hitachi Energy products: read the matching advisory. For RUGGEDCOM APE1808, upgrade PAN-OS to a corrected version, restrict network access to the device and keep it off the internet.
exec: Routine but relevant for operators of Siemens industrial gear; one network appliance flaw is rated critical and reachable without a login.
plain: The US cyber agency published six warnings about security flaws in Siemens and Hitachi Energy equipment used to run buildings, factories and power systems.

key_findings: CISA released six ICS advisories on November 12: five Siemens advisories and an update to one for Hitachi Energy RTU500.
Siemens products named are Building Automation and Energy products, Desigo, Gridscale, Industrial Edge Management and RUGGEDCOM APE1808.
ICSA-26-316-04 covers CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder in PAN-OS on RUGGEDCOM APE1808, rated CVSS 9.8, with all versions listed as affected.
A remote unauthenticated attacker could send a crafted compressed stream to leak memory, cause denial of service or possibly execute code; the advisory does not say whether it is exploited.
Only the bulletin and ICSA-26-316-04 were read; details of the other five advisories are not captured here.
recommendations: Upgrade PAN-OS on RUGGEDCOM APE1808 to a corrected version and apply the upstream workarounds.
Restrict network access to the devices and follow Siemens' industrial security operating guidelines.
Keep control system devices off the internet and behind firewalls, isolated from business networks.
Use up-to-date VPNs where remote access is needed.

sources.name: CISA bulletin: Six Industrial Control Systems Advisories

summary: CISA released six industrial control system advisories on November 12: five for Siemens products (building automation and energy, Desigo and Gridscale, Industrial Edge Management and two for RUGGEDCOM APE1808) and an update for Hitachi Energy RTU500. One RUGGEDCOM advisory covers a Brotli decoder flaw in the bundled PAN-OS, rated 9.8, that a remote unauthenticated attacker could use to crash the device or possibly run code.
title: CISA: six industrial control advisories cover Siemens building, edge and RUGGEDCOM products

validation.note: Reviewed against the original CISA document. The bulletin and ICSA-26-316-04 were read; the other five advisory pages would not load.
